title: Metric Alignment v1
description: An agent's mapping between an idea card's metric names and the identifiers of the project's locked protocol. Produced because the two names come from different model calls with no shared vocabulary: ideation writes prose ('unseen-domain top-1 accuracy (held-out domain)') while the protocol carries an identifier with its definition attached ('target_unseen_domain_top1_accuracy (held-out domain value, all samples, %)'). Deciding whether those are the same measurement is a judgement, so it is asked of an agent — but the agent may only choose among the protocol identifiers it was given or say it does not match, because a guessed rename would silently change what an experiment claims to measure. `evidence` per mapping is required: an alignment that cannot quote the protocol's own definition is a guess and must stay unresolved.

cardMetric.description: The metric as the idea card declares it, verbatim.

protocolMetric.description: One of the protocol identifiers handed to the call, or null when the card metric measures something the protocol does not define. Never a new name: inventing one is how a primary metric changes silently.

reasoning.description: Why these are or are not the same measurement, naming the part that decides it (population, split, aggregation), not restating the two strings.

evidence.description: Quoted text from the protocol definition and/or the card the verdict rests on.

unmeasuredProtocolMetrics.description: Protocol identifiers no card metric covers. These are what the idea would still fail to report, so the gap stays visible instead of being smoothed over.

summary.description: One paragraph a researcher can act on: what aligned, what did not, and what has to change if the disagreement is real (revisit the card, or re-lock the protocol deliberately).
